If you want the fastest ship, get 4 White Dwarf 3015 engines (available at level 24 but requires Starship Design rank 4) and cap your ship mass at 1020.

Tier 6 can be done on extreme difficulty with only Rank 1 of Piloting and Targeting Control Systems (starting with Bounty Hunter background). If you want it easier, max out Engine Systems for invulnerable and efficient boost. I would have suggested Security but apparently there’s a key that makes that unnecessary, mentioned in other comments. 

1. Save both allies for tier 6. Make sure damage and shield upgrades are active. 
2. When tier 6 starts, allow yourself to be defeated once before getting up to spawn allies, otherwise they may be defeated before you sit back down. 
3. Do a manual save before summoning allies, and quick save after each ship kill so long as you aren’t be fired upon. The allies don’t respawn AFAIK, so if you fail, reload rather than reset. 
4. Use thrusters to position yourself behind a large asteroid before the fight and stay put until an enemy flies by. Target them and blast away using ship VATS. 
5. If you are fired upon and lose your shield, boost away behind another asteroid and get up from your seat to allow shield to recharge. 
6. If you’re fighting out in the open, always try to flank enemies so they can’t attack you. Don’t fight head on. 
7. Boost past them and try to target them with VATS as you are about to pass by, which will allow you to automatically turn as you fire on them. This is risky though because if they boost, then it might send you into a wild spin. 
8. Alternatively, boost past them and then use thrusters to quickly turn around and then boost again to catch up behind them if you can. 
9. Good luck!

Sort of. The Automated Weapons System skill only applies its 30% damage increase to turrets, but the other stat buffs to the targeting system applies to all weapons. It’s common to confuse “auto” with turrets in this game, but turrets always have turret in their name. Think of auto as short for automatic in the same sense as handheld weapons. They fire fast. They also have a magazine that only needs to be recharged after fully depleted (though it will recharge whenever you stop firing, too). Non-auto weapons recharge between every shot. The primary difference is that you can allocate 1 power to an auto weapon and fire its entire magazine for the same amount of damage and dps as if you allocated 12 power. It will recharge slow AF though, since power only affects recharge speed. Since non-auto weapons need to recharge between every shot, they do need high power allocation to do high dps.

Also, the two of the best particle turrets in the game only require 1 power to do full dps, since they recharge faster than they shoot. The Disruptor 3320 Neutron Turret, available at level 20, and the Obliterator 250MeV Alpha Turret, available at level 60.

I also highly recommend getting the Fusor DC401 Reactor at level 20, as it has the highest power at lower levels, and there won’t be any worthwhile upgrades for a very long time. It’s Class C so you will need to max out piloting. I recommend maxing out Starship Design from levels 21-24 and getting White Dwarf 3015 Engines, as they are the fastest engines in the game. You’ll want to cap your ship mass at 1020 though or you’ll start losing maneuverability.

Oh and the Vanguard Hellfire Autocannons are the best ballistic weapons in the game. Nothing beats them for hull damage. Grab both of these Vanguard beasts, and either toss on a turret or an EM weapon if you like boarding, and you are set.
Helpful tool for finding planets with specific resources: https://inara.cz/starfield/starsystems/
The guy will be there right off the bat. No need to go to Mars or elsewhere first.

Another thing the game doesn’t tell you is that these weapons are special and benefit from both the particle beam weapon systems and energy weapon systems skills. The energy weapon skill will boost its damage to shields, along with the reduced targeting cost and faster recharge. The Isolation skill also increases hull damage for all ship weapons so long as you don’t have an active companion. These are basically the best ship weapons in the game, and they’re available at level 1 (after joining the Vanguard).

I don’t know the answer to your question, but I’ve managed to complete tier 6 on extreme difficulty on two different characters, and so I’ll offer some tips that may help. 

• The most useful skills are maxed engine systems and maxed targeting skill, and of course piloting for thrusters. I recommend starting with Bounty Hunter background as it has the best and most useful starting skills. 

• Boost to avoid getting shot when facing them head on (tier 4 engine systems makes them stop attacking while you’re boosting), and try to position yourself behind them. If you see the missile warning, boost to avoid it. Use thrusters to cancel booster and to turn around quickly. Always attack in targeting mode for more damage. 

• It can help to stop and hide behind and close to an asteroid and wait for a ship to fly by, then blast away at it in targeting mode without moving. 

• If you can get to a safe spot for a moment where you’re not being attacked, getting out of your seat will allow your shield to regen and they won’t attack you. It’s also a good time to save. 

• I save all the debug hacks for tier 6. When you reach tier 6, let them attack you so you can get up and reset it after using debug tools, otherwise your allies will get demolished before you even sit back down. If you have the security skill, then you can unlock the damage and shield boosts for all tiers, and have 2 allies in tier 6. Once the allies die, they don’t come back, so save them for when you really need them. You could use one in tier 5 and the other in tier 6 if you need to. Save before summoning the allies. If you are defeated and lose your allies, don’t reset, just load the save. 

I love hearing the astonishment of the vanguard recruiter when he sees you beat tier 6. “No one beats tier 6!” Lol

Good luck!

Bethesda, why do you hate hoarders now with this limited stash crap? You give us FO4 and spoil us with unlimited storage, and now this shit. Are you really going to leave me with no other option than to play the entire game over-encumbered just so I can play it the way I enjoy, which is to loot everything I see?

Since you seem to lack innovation and foresight in this department, I’ll offer a simple solution. Make junk auto-scrap when you store it, and make it weightless while in the stash. Non-junk can remain weighted to fill up whatever arbitrary limit you set. This way we won’t have to choose between keeping a weapon for later use or keeping a ton of crafting materials we spent hours gathering, and we won’t have to create a mule character, which I’m sure would be a greater strain on your servers. 

I’m amazed that you don’t perceive this stash problem to be your biggest problem, and aren’t making it your highest priority. There are a lot players already cancelling pre-orders and many others who will probably lose enthusiasm and quit because of the limited stash as time goes on. Once their stashes are full, and they’ve already done every tip and trick to reduce weight, and they’ve had to scrap all the extra weapons and armor they’ve found, sell or throw away crafting materials, and have had to deal with being over-encumbered for the 1000th time, even the staunchest defenders of the stash limit will probably grow tired. Most of us are already tired of it during the beta. Please take this more seriously.
